investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-29T00:56–01:03Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state, so the eval runner could not advance past agent creation.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. The other 4 nodes are ineligible due to node affinity or selector constraints. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free slots (no lower-priority victims found), every new remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner calls createAgent with machineType "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885), the pod is never scheduled, and the probe times out after ~144–147 s without writing any evidence, causing all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to remain missing.

possibleCauses: Primary: The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes, leaving no schedulable capacity for new remote-agent pods. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority pods are present on those nodes.

Secondary: The node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a subset of nodes (only 2 of 6 carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource), amplifying the impact of any capacity shortfall.

Tertiary: A recent increase in concurrent remote-agent demand (e.g., from parallel eval runs or production load) may have consumed the available VM slots before the eval probes ran. No traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm this.

Lower confidence: A node or VM pool configuration change may have reduced the number of nodes advertising kata.peerpods.io/vm, shrinking available capacity. No suspect changes are listed in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges, so this remains speculative.

This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits." investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API returned a hard billing limit error (billing_hard_limit_reached) when the eval runner called /api/generate/image/stream. The stream terminated with a generation_error frame instead of a generation_completed frame, causing both required contract assertions to fail: frameTypes did not contain "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent remained false.

When the runner called /api/generate/image/stream (evidence: source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1977-1985, line 1984), the upstream OpenAI image generation API rejected the request with error code "billing_hard_limit_reached" and type "billing_limit_user_error". This caused the server to emit a generation_error frame with GENERATION_FAILED instead of completing the stream with a generation_completed frame and an artifact URL. The eval contract (expected-output.contract) requires frameTypes to contain "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent to equal true, both of which are impossible while the billing limit remains in effect. This is an eval infrastructure / external dependency failure; no evidence of user-traffic or production incident signals is present in the packet.

investigation.title: published-observability-snapshot eval fail: status.json is stale by 717 minutes (contract max: 300)
investigation.summary: The eval fetched the published snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json and measured its age as 717 minutes, which is 2.39× the contract maximum of 300 minutes. This is an eval-layer failure against the published-observability-snapshot expected-output contract; no sibling public-website checks failed, and no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing status.json at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not produced a fresh snapshot in at least 717 minutes. The contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (line 482) requires snapshotAgeMinutes <= 300. The snapshot itself is structurally valid (all 12 required evidence fields present, source="github-actions", hasLiveSource=true, featureCount=19), so the failure is isolated to freshness: the workflow that writes and publishes the file either did not run, failed silently, or its published output was not updated on the GitHub Pages branch.
proof: failed-check.message: contractValidationError = 'snapshotAgeMinutes expected <= 300 but got 717' — the sole violated assertion.
failed-check.evidence: snapshotAgeMinutes=717, maxAgeMinutes=300, source='github-actions', hasLiveSource=true, generatedAtPresent=true — snapshot is structurally intact but stale.
expected-output.contract: assertion { path: 'snapshotAgeMinutes', max: 300 } defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482.

source.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:2168-2170: runner fetches the live URL via publicJsonUrl(args.publishedSnapshotUrl) and derives snapshotAgeMinutes from the payload, confirming the age value reflects the actual published file's timestamp.
sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all three sibling checks passed, ruling out a broad public-website or hosting outage.
source.check-config.published-observability-snapshot: check is marked required=false, statusImpact='informational', confirming this is an eval-layer signal, not a required-check outage.
possibleCauses: Most likely — GitHub Actions workflow that generates and publishes status.json did not run or was skipped for the past ~12 hours (717 minutes), leaving the stale file on the GitHub Pages branch.
Workflow ran but failed before writing or committing the updated status.json, so the old file remained published.
Workflow ran and committed successfully but the GitHub Pages deployment step failed or was throttled, so the CDN/Pages layer still serves the old file.
A schedule trigger for the snapshot-generation workflow was accidentally disabled, removed, or its cron expression was changed such that it no longer fires at the expected cadence.
The workflow ran but targeted a different branch or path than the one served at the snapshotUrl, causing the published file to go unrefreshed.

investigations.title: image-generation-stream Eval Failure: OpenAI Billing Hard Limit Reached on /api/generate/image/stream
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API returned a hard billing limit error (billing_hard_limit_reached) when the eval runner called /api/generate/image/stream. The stream terminated with a generation_error frame instead of a generation_completed frame, causing both required contract assertions to fail: frameTypes did not contain "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent remained false.
investigations.rootCause: The OpenAI account or API key used by the eval runner has hit its configured billing hard limit. When the runner called /api/generate/image/stream (evidence: source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1977-1985, line 1984), the upstream OpenAI image generation API rejected the request with error code "billing_hard_limit_reached" and type "billing_limit_user_error". This caused the server to emit a generation_error frame with GENERATION_FAILED instead of completing the stream with a generation_completed frame and an artifact URL. The eval contract (expected-output.contract) requires frameTypes to contain "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent to equal true, both of which are impossible while the billing limit remains in effect. This is an eval infrastructure / external dependency failure; no evidence of user-traffic or production incident signals is present in the packet.
proof: failed-check.message: generation_error frame data contains the verbatim OpenAI error: {"message": "Billing hard limit has been reached.", "type": "billing_limit_user_error", "code": "billing_hard_limit_reached"}
failed-check.evidence: observed frameTypes are [generation_start, generation_start, generation_progress, generation_error, message] — generation_completed is absent and imageUrlPresent is false

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=1012, indicating the request was rejected almost immediately by the upstream API rather than timing out, consistent with a billing rejection rather than a network or server-side processing failure

expected-output.contract: assertions require frameTypes contains "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent equals true — both violated as a direct consequence of the billing error terminating the stream early

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1977-1985 (line 1984): eval runner calls apiSse to /api/generate/image/stream, confirming the exact endpoint that received the billing rejection

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1978-1986 (line 1986): runner uses model process.env.AURA_STATUS_IMAGE_MODEL || "gpt-image-2", confirming the OpenAI image model being billed against
possibleCauses: Primary: The OpenAI account or API key configured for the eval environment has reached its hard spending limit, causing all image generation requests to be rejected at the billing layer before any generation work begins.
Secondary: The API key used by the eval runner is scoped to a project or organization that has a separate, lower billing limit than the main production key, and that limit has been exhausted.
Tertiary: A billing limit was set too low for the volume of eval runs (e.g., nightly scheduled runs accumulating cost), causing the limit to be hit during this run cycle.

Lower probability: The AURA_STATUS_IMAGE_MODEL environment variable is set to a model with a different billing tier that exhausted a model-specific quota, though the error type billing_limit_user_error points to an account-level hard cap rather than a per-model quota.

investigations.title: model-matrix eval failure: aura-gpt-5-5 returns 502/424 provider_account_unavailable
investigations.summary: The model-matrix eval failed because the aura-gpt-5-5 model returned a 502 bad-gateway wrapping a 424 Failed Dependency with error code provider_account_unavailable, causing 1 of 2 models to fail and violating the allPassed=true and failedModelCount=0 assertions. The sibling model aura-claude-sonnet-4-6 passed cleanly, isolating the failure to the aura-gpt-5-5 provider path only.
investigations.rootCause: AURA's backend was temporarily unable to reach the upstream model provider for aura-gpt-5-5 at the time of the eval run (2026-07-29T00:55:42Z). The runtime test endpoint POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test returned HTTP 502 containing a 424 Failed Dependency with error code provider_account_unavailable and the message "AURA is temporarily unable to reach the model provider. This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits." This is a provider-side or AURA-side connectivity/availability issue scoped to the aura-gpt-5-5 model route, not an eval infrastructure defect and not a user account or credits problem. No sibling checks failed, no shared dependency failure was detected, and the eval infrastructure itself (evidence collection, runner, contract validation) functioned correctly.

possibleCauses: Most likely: Transient upstream provider unavailability for the aura-gpt-5-5 model provider at the time of the eval run, as explicitly stated in the 424 error message ('AURA is temporarily unable to reach the model provider. This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits.').
Possible: A sustained or recurring outage or degradation on the provider side for the model backing aura-gpt-5-5, which would cause repeated eval failures across runs.

Possible: A misconfiguration or missing provider account/credential binding for aura-gpt-5-5 in the desktop-release runtime environment, causing the provider resolution to fail (provider=null, resolvedModel=null in the evidence).

Less likely: A routing or gateway-layer regression in AURA's backend that prevents the runtime test harness from reaching the aura-gpt-5-5 provider endpoint, while leaving the anthropic/aura-claude-sonnet-4-6 route unaffected.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-29T00:56–01:03Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state, so the eval runner could not advance past agent creation.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. The other 4 nodes are ineligible due to node affinity or selector constraints. investigations.title: published-observability-snapshot eval fail: status.json is stale by 717 minutes (contract max: 300)
investigations.summary: The eval fetched the published snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json and measured its age as 717 minutes, which is 2.39× the contract maximum of 300 minutes. This is an eval-layer failure against the published-observability-snapshot expected-output contract; no sibling public-website checks failed, and no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing status.json at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not produced a fresh snapshot in at least 717 minutes. The contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (line 482) requires snapshotAgeMinutes <= 300. The snapshot itself is structurally valid (all 12 required evidence fields present, source="github-actions", hasLiveSource=true, featureCount=19), so the failure is isolated to freshness: the workflow that writes and publishes the file either did not run, failed silently, or its published output was not updated on the GitHub Pages branch.

failed-check.evidence: snapshotAgeMinutes=717, maxAgeMinutes=300, source='github-actions', hasLiveSource=true, generatedAtPresent=true — snapshot is structurally intact but stale.
expected-output.contract: assertion { path: 'snapshotAgeMinutes', max: 300 } defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482.

source.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:2168-2170: runner fetches the live URL via publicJsonUrl(args.publishedSnapshotUrl) and derives snapshotAgeMinutes from the payload, confirming the age value reflects the actual published file's timestamp.
sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all three sibling checks passed, ruling out a broad public-website or hosting outage.
source.check-config.published-observability-snapshot: check is marked required=false, statusImpact='informational', confirming this is an eval-layer signal, not a required-check outage.
possibleCauses: Most likely — GitHub Actions workflow that generates and publishes status.json did not run or was skipped for the past ~12 hours (717 minutes), leaving the stale file on the GitHub Pages branch.
Workflow ran but failed before writing or committing the updated status.json, so the old file remained published.
Workflow ran and committed successfully but the GitHub Pages deployment step failed or was throttled, so the CDN/Pages layer still serves the old file.
A schedule trigger for the snapshot-generation workflow was accidentally disabled, removed, or its cron expression was changed such that it no longer fires at the expected cadence.
The workflow ran but targeted a different branch or path than the one served at the snapshotUrl, causing the published file to go unrefreshed.
